paper.title: A general modular framework for gene set enrichment analysis
paper.citation: Ackermann M, Strimmer K. A general modular framework for gene set enrichment analysis. BMC Bioinformatics 10:47 (2009)

shared_data.what: Each simulated data set is analysed with every combination of modules; the paper simulated 100 data sets per combination
shared_data.sensitivity: The paper's Tables 2, 3 and 4 print the same squared mod.t / mean / resampling cell, so it shared data there too. On squared statistics maxmean equals the mean, so our maxmean column repeats the mean column; the paper's differ by up to 0.04 (set 9), as separate data would.

seeds.what: Seeds 20090203 + replicate for the data and 20090203 + 100000 + replicate for the random gene sets and label permutations (1000 of each, shared by the combinations of a replicate)
seeds.sensitivity: The paper gives no seeds. Any seed changes each rate by Monte Carlo error only; the tolerance of every field is a 99% two-proportion band for two shares of 100 (gseamod::rate_tolerance).

background.what: The background genes of sets 3, 4, 5, 8 and 9 are drawn at random for each set and each replicate
background.sensitivity: The paper says 'selected randomly' without saying whether the draws overlap; overlaps change no expected rate.

one_sided.what: Every test is one-sided (large statistics enriched) and its p-value is the share of null statistics at or above the observed one
one_sided.sensitivity: Without transformation set 3 lies below random sets of all 600 genes (40 up-shifted genes raise their mean), so a one-sided test never calls it, as in the paper's 0.00; a two-sided test would.

binary.what: The binary transformation calls a gene at two-sided p <= 0.05 (t distribution for t and mod.t, Fisher's z for correlations)
binary.sensitivity: The paper gives no cutoff. Calling genes at local fdr <= 0.2 (fdrtool) instead calls almost no gene and drops the detection rates far below the paper's (variant binary_lfdr02 in tables.json).

lfdr.what: Local fdr from fdrtool with a normal null for t and mod.t and a correlation null for correlations; the transformed score is 1 - lfdr
lfdr.sensitivity: Not varied. fdrtool is the second author's package; the paper does not say which null was used.

condfdr.what: Cond. FDR statistic: the mean over the set of 1 - fdr_S, with fdr_S(z) = fdr(z) (m/N) / pi_S(z), fdr from fdrtool on the untransformed statistic and pi_S from a linear logistic regression of set membership on the transformed statistic
condfdr.sensitivity: The paper names only the logistic regression. Its slope alone is a monotone function of the set's score sum, so it gives exactly the mean's p-values under resampling (variant condslope), while the paper's cond. FDR column differs from its mean column.

parametric.what: Parametric null of the mean of squared statistics: m times the mean is chi-squared with m degrees of freedom (independent standard normal statistics)
parametric.sensitivity: The paper says only that the parametric null assumes independent genes; its rates (set 5: 0.85, near permutation's 0.90) point to a self-contained null like this one, not a competitive normal approximation.

hotelling.what: Hotelling T2 = t' R^-1 t with R the corpcor shrinkage correlation of the data centred within each class
hotelling.sensitivity: Centring over all samples (variant hotelling_overall) or shrinking the covariance instead (hotelling_cov) moves the correlated sets; see the cause of Table 6.

globaltest_version.what: globaltest 5.56.0 (Bioconductor 3.18) with a logistic model; the paper's 2008 version is not stated
globaltest_version.sensitivity: Its statistic equals ours up to a constant (checked), so only the parametric column depends on the version's asymptotic p-value.

p53_filter.what: p53 genes from GSEA's collapsed-symbol file (10,100 genes), kept when the maximum is at least 5 on the log2 scale and the max/min ratio is at least 2 (both criteria), then log2
p53_filter.sensitivity: The paper's wording allows either criterion and either file. Both criteria on the collapsed file give exactly 8,768 genes; either criterion keeps 10,100, the maximum alone 8,819; the probe-level file gives 10,743.

hedenfalk_map.what: Hedenfalk clones mapped to gene symbols through NCBI UniGene build 236 (2013, the last build): clones in exactly one UniGene cluster with a symbol, clones of one symbol averaged; C2 sets of 15 to 500 mapped genes (the size rule the paper states for p53)
hedenfalk_map.sensitivity: The paper's mapping (a 2008 UniGene build) and its choice of the 89 sets are not given. Ours gives 2,233 genes and 84 sets; sets of 10 or more genes give 160 sets.

real_draws.what: 1000 random gene sets per set size and 1000 label permutations for the p53 and Hedenfalk analyses (seeded)
real_draws.sensitivity: The paper states 1000 only for the simulation. Counts of sets near a cutoff move by Monte Carlo error.

read_bars.what: Bar heights of Figs 2 and 4 (right panels) read off the Springer original figures through the y-axis tick marks
read_bars.sensitivity: One pixel is 0.62 sets in Fig. 2 and 0.19 sets in Fig. 4. Fig. 4 readings lie within 0.18 of an integer; Fig. 2 readings within 0.40, so each Fig. 2 bar is compared with a tolerance of one set.

read_hist.what: Histogram counts of Fig. 3 read off the Springer original through the tick marks of both axes
read_hist.sensitivity: One count is 4.1 px (top) and 5.7 px (bottom); every reading lies within 0.16 of an integer and both histograms sum to exactly 290 sets.

cause.summary: 51 of 54 rates agree. Cond. FDR misses sets 8 and 9 (0.53 and 0.84 against 0.84 and 0.99) and ES misses set 8 (0.44 against 0.65): the paper does not define its cond. FDR statistic or its ES ordering on squared scores.

hypotheses.test: Variant condslope over the same 100 data sets
hypotheses.detail: The slope gives exactly the mean's p-values under resampling (set 8: 0.57, set 9: 0.92), not the paper's 0.84 and 0.99.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Cond. FDR is the mean over the set of 1 - fdr_S (Efron's conditional fdr from that regression)
hypotheses.detail: Set 8: 0.53, set 9: 0.84 against 0.84 and 0.99.

page.lede: The authors' R code is lost. We rebuilt every module from the paper as the R package gseamod, reran the simulation study ({replicates} data sets) and redid the p53 and Hedenfalk analyses. Of {attempted} results we tried, {exact} came back within their tolerance as printed, {agrees} agree, {partly} partly and {differs} differ.
page.tables_caption: Each rate is the share of 100 simulated data sets in which a set was significant at p <= 0.05. Neither the paper's seeds nor its code survive, so a rate matches when it lies in the 99% band for two shares of 100.
page.tables_note: Table 2, Table 4 and Table 5 came back within Monte Carlo error but for one rate, Table 5's set 3 parametric, which is 0.050 on 400 more data sets. Our cond. FDR misses sets 8 and 9 of Table 3, and our Hotelling finds the correlated set 1 more often than the paper's.
page.items_caption: Every figure, table and claim of the paper, with its verdict from results.json. Exact for a simulated rate means within its Monte Carlo band.
page.claims_line: The main claims hold: the mean of squared moderated t beats ES and Hotelling, and the simulation tables come back. The claims that do not match come from our cond. FDR, which is not the paper's, and from the Hedenfalk gene mapping.
came_back: Three gene-level statistics, five transformations, six gene set statistics, four significance assessments, globaltest and Hotelling, as the R package gseamod.
206 of 207 rates of Tables 2, 4 and 5 within Monte Carlo error; 51 of 54 in Table 3 and 25 of 27 in Table 6.
The paper's filter on GSEA's collapsed file gives exactly 8,768 genes and 290 sets of 15 to 321 genes.
Hotelling, globaltest, ES and maxmean within one set of the published bars at cutoff 0.01.
breast_cancer_estrogen_signalling first again, and 27 of the 41 sets at their printed p.
buried: The paper's cond. FDR statistic: neither of two readings of it gives its Table 3 or Fig. 2 numbers.
Its Hotelling correlation estimate: ours finds the correlated set 1 more often.
Its Hedenfalk gene mapping and its 89 sets: ours has 2,233 genes and 84 sets, and finds more sets.
The data behind Fig. 3: our within-set correlations run a little lower.
matched: Rates of 100 simulated data sets against the printed ones, each within a 99% band for two shares of 100.
Bars at cutoff 0.01 read off the original figure files through their tick marks.
Histogram counts read off the same way; both sum to 290 sets.
Each claim written as a comparison and checked first on the paper's own tables (22 of 22 hold there).
page.closing: Ackermann and Strimmer's modules came back as an R package.
